title: Georgekutty Comes Home to Your Living Room. Drishyam 3 Lands on Prime Video, and the Diaspora Can Finally See How the Lie Holds.
excerpt: Mohanlal's 231-crore monster — the highest-grossing Malayalam film of the year and the first South Indian title of 2026 to cross $10 million overseas — is now a click away.
body:
For four-and-a-half years of screen time, **Georgekutty** has been protecting a lie. For the rest of us, the wait has been shorter but no less anxious: how, exactly, does the most ordinary man in Malayalam cinema keep outsmarting people who hold every card? As of June 18, you no longer have to drive to a theatre to find out. **Drishyam 3** is streaming on **Amazon Prime Video**, and the franchise that turned a cable-TV salesman into India's most beloved liar has arrived in living rooms across the diaspora.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=07h9Y1XKBWI</youtube>

Let's be clear about what just landed on your watchlist. **Mohanlal**'s third outing as Georgekutty is not a quiet little Malayalam drama that snuck onto streaming. It is a phenomenon. Directed once again by **Jeethu Joseph**, the architect of the entire saga, the film has clawed past **231 crore worldwide**, become the highest-grossing Malayalam film of the year, and — in a stat that should make every regional-cinema sceptic blush — become the first South Indian film of 2026 to cross **$10 million overseas**. That overseas number is built almost entirely on diaspora shoulders: Malayali families in the Gulf, in London, in New Jersey, filling weekend shows for sixteen straight days.

The story picks up four and a half years after we last left the family, and Jeethu Joseph does what he does best — tightens the screws slowly. A wealthy but paranoid Georgekutty now faces a fresh conspiracy, this time engineered by Varun's father and a clutch of corrupt police officers determined to break the family from the inside. They go after his daughter, Anju. What follows is the franchise's signature pleasure: an ordinary man rearranging reality itself, manipulating crime scenes, staging injuries, bending the truth until it points anywhere but at his family. To say more would be a crime against the suspense the series has spent a decade building.

> The Drishyam franchise has built its reputation on one promise: just when you think you've worked out the trick, the floor moves.

What makes the streaming arrival genuinely exciting for NRI viewers is access. The theatrical run, for all its overseas muscle, still meant hunting for the one Saturday-night show within driving distance. Now Prime Video carries the film into homes from Sydney to Toronto, and crucially, the platform makes the suspense portable — pause it, rewind the reveal, watch Mohanlal's face do the heavy lifting in close-up. For families scattered across time zones, it's the rare release everyone can finally watch on the same weekend, group chat lit up with theories.

Mohanlal, for his part, has rarely been better. There is a stillness to his Georgekutty now — the weariness of a man who has been carrying the same secret for over a decade, who flinches at every knock on the door. Critics have singled out the performance as the film's spine, and it is: the plot machinery only thrills because we believe, completely, in the exhausted ordinariness of the man operating it. Jeethu Joseph expands the universe — more players, higher stakes, a darker palette — without ever losing the kitchen-table intimacy that made the first film a sensation back in 2013.

The theatrical timeline tells its own story of restraint. Prime Video confirmed the digital premiere a full four weeks after the cinema release, a window that let the film bank its overseas millions before opening the gates. By its third Friday the box office had naturally cooled — 0.80 crore on day sixteen — which is precisely when a streaming drop makes sense: catch the long tail, hand the film to everyone who couldn't make it out.

For the diaspora, *Drishyam* has always been more than a thriller. It's a story about how far a parent will go, about family closing ranks against a hostile world — themes that land differently when you're watching from a country that isn't home. That it's now a single click away, dubbed and subtitled for audiences who don't speak Malayalam, only widens the circle.

**Where to watch:** *Drishyam 3* is streaming now on **Amazon Prime Video** in India and across international markets including the US, UK, Canada, and the Gulf. The film is available in Malayalam with subtitles, and Prime typically carries Telugu, Tamil, and Kannada audio options for the franchise — check your regional library. If you've somehow stayed unspoiled this long, clear an evening, silence the group chat, and let Georgekutty do what he does best.
